fields.Name: International Cheese Federation News Archive
fields.Description: This page from the International Cheese Federation features a collection of recent news articles and updates. Topics include regulatory compliance for small producers, environmental factors affecting cheese maturation, market pricing trends, member profiles, judge accreditation processes, federal labeling standards, raw milk cheese regulations, food safety certifications (HACCP), and supply chain resilience. The content highlights the federation's focus on advocacy, education, and industry news.

Four months until the small-producer deadline

The deadline behind the two-dollar block 

 

Block cheese has held above two dollars a pound for most of the month, and the federal margin coverage window that was supposed to close last week now closes this Friday instead.

The distributor rep who still shows up to committee calls 

 

A regional sales director spends his days moving other people’s cheese, not making it — and he’s stayed on federation committee calls for years, for reasons that have less to do with sales than you’d guess.

The two scorecards a judge learns to read 

 

Competition Judge Accreditation asks members to score a cheese two different ways in the same sitting — once for what’s wrong with it, once for what’s right — and most candidates find the second harder.

Yuri Lee 




 


What ‘aged’ actually has to mean on the label 

 

Federal standards fix the name on a lot of cheese labels, but words like ‘aged,’ ‘farmstead,’ and ‘raw milk’ aren’t pinned down the same way — and members want that gap closed. 


Continue Reading

Sep 



 


 

 

Advocacy 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


The 60-day line, and who’s asking to move it 

 

The federal rule letting raw-milk cheese cross state lines only after 60 days of aging hasn’t moved in decades. Members are split on whether it should.

The plan behind the plan: what the HACCP credential actually covers 

 

Members keep asking whether the Food Safety & HACCP Certificate duplicates their existing food safety plan. It doesn’t — here’s what it adds.

What a slow-moving storm does to a cheese supply chain 

 

A slow-moving hurricane’s crawl up the East Coast reminded distributors and small creameries alike that a cold chain has more weak links than a rind has cracks.
